chunks.heading: Was I Good Enough
chunks.notes: Opens with childhood memory of watching anime and dodging deadlines/self, then pivots on the repeated rhetorical question "Was I good enough?"

chunks.heading: Was I Good Enough
chunks.notes: Splits the self into "me, myself, and I" as three shadows/voices that argue in the mirror, alternating good and bad days, all circling the same worth question.

chunks.heading: Was I Good Enough
chunks.notes: Moves from an inner "door only I can hear" slamming into direct flashback memories of a yelling mother, an absent father, and an angry brother.

chunks.heading: Was I Good Enough
chunks.notes: Describes carrying childhood weight quietly, then a felt shift toward small daily gratitudes that end each stanza on a landing line about proof of enoughness.

chunks.heading: Was I Good Enough
chunks.notes: The poem's turn/climax -- explicitly rejecting "self-help ... guru garbage" and declaring self-companionship and trust, landing on "finally enough."

chunks.heading: Was I Good Enough
chunks.notes: Closes with a cluster of rhetorical questions about choosing oneself, then lands the poem's final aphorism redefining love as daily self-choosing, echoing the title's original question.
